sense.text:
“Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement.” The tenth day of the seventh month is the day we are in, the day of atonement. To atone is to make amends or reparation, restitution. Amends for what? For your sins. And amends to who? To your God, and also to whoever you have a problem with. You got to make amends with them too.

“It shall be an holy convocation unto you.” A convocation is a large formal assembly of people: an assembly, a gathering, a meeting. So the day of atonement is a holy gathering, and God commands us to come together on it. It is not a day to just stay in the house and sleep. All praise to the Most High that we come together every day of atonement and hold classes.

“And ye shall afflict your souls.” The scripture is telling you how to keep the day. To afflict your soul is not beating yourself with a whip, the way some do. It is fasting: not eating and not tasting anything. And don’t stuff yourself with a big plate of food and a big bottle of water right before the fast so you won’t feel it the next day. That takes away from what the fast is meant to be. You are supposed to be hungry, you are supposed to be thirsty: you are afflicting your soul. Drink a lot of water and eat fruits beforehand, especially in the summertime, but don’t be stuffing your belly.

Those that are sick and must take medication, that is between them and the Lord. If it is for your life and you need it, you will not be told not to take it, but no one can be told to break the least of the commandments either.

“And offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.” Are we supposed to offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord today? No. The only thing we don’t do anymore is the animal sacrifice, because Christ is our atonement.

“And ye shall do no work in that same day: for it is a day of atonement.” On the day of atonement you are not to work. Don’t call and ask if it is okay to work because your boss would not give you off. It is not okay. Every one of God’s sabbaths, the new moons and the feast days, is a day of rest, and the calendar is given at the beginning of the year, so those with jobs can put in for the days they need off.

If you try to get it off and you are not able to, the Lord knows your heart: we are in captivity. But if you had the power to get it off and you didn’t, God knows your heart too, and he knows you’re full of crap. That is why the scripture says let every man work out his own salvation.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul”. Israel puts fasting and afflicting the soul side by side: when you are fasting, that is afflicting your soul.

So when Leviticus commands “ye shall afflict your souls” on the day of atonement, it is commanding a fast.

Here is the precept of how you afflict your soul. The king of Nineveh proclaimed, “Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water”. Afflicting your soul means not eating anything and not tasting anything, not even drinking water.

Not tasting anything also means you don’t brush your teeth that day. Brush your teeth before the fast begins. Some will say, I’m going out in public and I want my breath smelling right, but the fast is between you and God.

“But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way”. It is you crying out to the Lord while you are afflicting your soul.

Some do water fasts for health reasons, and that is a different fast. The fast of the day of atonement, you cannot eat or drink anything.

“And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.” Christ fasted and he was hungry. When you fast, you don’t eat anything.

But none of you try to fast forty days and forty nights and drop down dead. You are not on the level Christ was on, and then the authorities come asking who told this man to fast forty days. Don’t be doing stupid stuff. Be very mindful.

This is how to deal with children on the day of atonement. “And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way”. You teach your children the commandments, sitting in your house and walking with them.

Can you teach a two-year-old anything? Does a six-month-old have understanding? Use your common sense. Don’t starve the baby. The baby can still have formula and milk. Years ago a man with some other Israelite group tried a ten-day fast with his daughters and they died, and the organization was blamed. If you starve your baby, ACS will show up at your door and you will go to jail, and don’t call us. Damn dummy.

The key thing is that the child must have understanding: you must be able to talk to the child. An eleven-year-old can be asked what day it is and say atonement, fasting for his sins. And when he says he has no sin, he is lying: evil is bound in the heart of a child, so he goes to God and asks for forgiveness.

Every child is different. Some start fasting at five, some at six, seven or eight. Explain to them what the fast is about, start them off with half a day, let them practise on the fasts kept twice a month, and let them build it up. It is up to the parents’ discretion, but do not be starving little kids.

“Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.” Due benevolence is sex. “The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.”

“Defraud ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer”. When you fast, you cannot have sex. Afflicting your soul includes no sex. And don’t be trying to get one in before the fast.

Remember in Exodus the Lord told them to make themselves clean and not come near their wives when they were coming before him. There is something spiritual in that. We have to learn to control even that appetite.

“Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.”

“Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so”. That is why no leader can tell you it is okay to work on any of God’s sabbaths, or give you permission to break God’s laws. And all the teachers must do the same and say no. You start from the least, and then it is this and that, and now he’s saying it’s okay. That is not how we roll. We have not been in the law for nothing.

So it is between you and the Lord, whether it is your job on the day of atonement or the medication you take.

“Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past”. The fast Paul is talking about is the day of atonement. Paul kept the day of atonement.

So are we supposed to keep the day of atonement today? Yes. Our forefathers kept it, Paul and the apostles kept it, and we are still to fast and afflict our soul. The only thing we no longer do is the animal sacrifice.

This goes back to the children. “And when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments, which the Lord our God hath commanded you? Then thou shalt say unto thy son, We were Pharaoh’s bondmen in Egypt”.

The son is speaking to you. He has understanding; he is able to conversate and ask, Dad, why are we doing this? That is a child you can bring into the fast. A baby going goo-goo ga-ga is not.

So don’t turn around and say a leader told you to starve your kid. Anyone starving a baby on the day of atonement will be put out of the school. We cannot play with crazy people who will put us on the news and let us be blamed for their stupidity.

sense.text: “Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation”. This is David praying to the Lord. He asks to be delivered from bloodguiltiness because David was guilty of murder.
“O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall shew forth thy praise.” We are to praise God, brothers and sisters. We have to train ourselves and learn to do that.
“For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” God desires not sacrifice. That is what you have to understand.

“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit”. The sacrifice God is looking for is a broken spirit. A broken spirit is when you do something wrong and you feel bad for what you did. You feel hurt inside: why did I do that, what the hell is wrong with me, I’m sorry. You really feel sorry for what you did.

“A broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” If you go to the Lord with a broken spirit and a broken heart, meaning you feel bad for what you did, he is not going to reject you.

precepts.why:
“For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation”. That broken and contrite spirit is godly sorrow: you are sorry for the evil you did against your God or your brother. If you have godly sorrow you are going to repent, and you are going to get the kingdom. Godly sorrow is being sorry for what you did and stopping.

“Not to be repented of” means you are not going back to the same thing. It is not that you repent of something and have to go repent of it again.

“But the sorrow of the world worketh death.” The sorrow of the world is being sorry because you got caught, not because what you did was wrong. Everybody found out, your head is down and you’re like, damn. That is not what God is looking for.

Godly sorrow is the broken and contrite spirit God wants to see in us when we come before him asking forgiveness of our sins.

“Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.” God sets our sins before him. He can see all of them. You can hide it from men, but God sees it.

Today is the day of atonement and we are making amends for our sins. Many of us have secret sins we are dealing with: some in the midst of fornication, some dealing with prostitutes, some hating each other, some watching porn. It is secret to us, but it is always before God’s eyes. Every last one of us battles secret sins within, and on this day of atonement you have to get rid of it. That is what atonement is.

sense.text:
“The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deeds of man as the apple of the eye”. The good deeds a man does, God keeps as the apple of his eye. The brothers that do good in this truth and help in this work, in the booster club, helping the travels: the Lord sees your alms, and they are as a signet before the Most High.

“And give repentance to his sons and daughters.” The Lord is going to give repentance to your sons and daughters.
“Afterwards he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompence upon their heads.” God is going to reward us if we do what is right.

“But unto them that repent, he granted them return”. Those of us that repent, the Lord will allow to return. That is what we are all here for: we want to be back in the Lord’s good graces, but we have to atone, we have to make amends.

“And comforted those that failed in patience.” He will comfort us even when we fail. In this walk you are going to fall a couple of times, but the Most High is going to comfort you.

“Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins”. We have to return unto the Lord and forsake our sins. Many are new among us and dealing with many things; some are online keeping the feast and fasting even though they don’t come to the school yet.

“Make thy prayer before his face, and offend less.” That is the key thing: offend less. You are going to offend; you are going to fall and make mistakes. But it is not the same mistake repeatedly, the same thing all the damn time. One day the devil whoops your behind; you get back up.

The high calling of God is without repentance. When you come to the truth you come with a lot of demons inside you and a lot of sins. Now you are learning you are Israel and learning the commandments, so you start cutting those sins off little by little, and offend less and less and less.

“Turn again to the most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead thee out of darkness into the light of health”.

“And hate thou abomination vehemently.” Vehemently is aggressively, forcefully, passionately, in an intense manner with great feeling. To hate evil vehemently is something you have to train yourself to do, because sin is pleasurable, but the Lord says the sin you are committing is abomination.

For example, the Bible teaches that a woman should not wear what pertains unto a man: pants. At work you see females in pants showing their shape and figure, and you don’t hate it; you’re like, damn. Should we be like that? No. It should not entice you. The society we grew up in is all we see, and it corrupts our mind and our way of thinking, so we have to train ourselves over time to hate these abominations vehemently. As Lot was vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” This is what it means that the Lord comforts those that fail in patience. In this walk, Israel, you are going to make mistakes and fall a couple of times, but you have that patience, and the Most High is going to comfort you.

The key thing is that when you fall, you never stay down. Some were caught up in fornication and were put out of the school, but they kept hanging on, still taking their notes and sending offerings, stopped the fornication, and were allowed back. When you fall, don’t just give up and go back into the world. Keep fighting to do what is right.

The wicked falls into mischief: when he falls, he goes back into the world and is evil. But the righteous, even if he falls, gets back up.

sense.text: “Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment”. The law says thou shalt not kill, and if you kill you are in danger of the judgment.

“That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”. There is no reason for you to be angry with your brother, you just don’t like that dude. You are in danger of the same judgment as thou shalt not kill, because that is hatred.

“And whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council”. The council is being brought before judgment, before two or three witnesses. “But whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.” Now you are cursing everybody out.

Christ took it to another level: you heard thou shalt not murder, but if you have secret hatred you are in danger of hellfire. You cannot secretly hate your brother or your wife and expect to get the kingdom.

“Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar”. The gift is the sacrifice you bring for your sins. “And there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee”. To keep remembering the evil your brother did against you means there are unresolved issues there. That is called a grudge.

A grudge is hatred, and it is something you cannot see. It is in somebody’s mind; it is secret. For months, for years you are around this brother, but inside you secretly carry something against him. A grudge is secret hatred, and there is no way to tell it if you are not spiritual.

“Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.” Leave the sacrifice there and go fix it with your brother first; then come and ask for forgiveness and offer your gift.

This is not for the day of atonement alone. Many wait for the day of atonement and call everybody saying, if I offended you in anything, can you forgive me? No. If you did something to somebody, you know what you did. You must acknowledge what you did: I’m sorry for stealing from you; I was bad-talking you, and I’m sorry for that. When problems come between you, fix them. If it festers too long it becomes a grudge and secret hatred.

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” To rebuke your neighbour is what Matthew 5 just showed: if he did something against you, go to him and talk to him about it. The rebuke is correcting your brother.

“Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people”. It is a commandment that we take no vengeance on our own brothers, our own people, and carry no grudges against them. A grudge is secret hatred: you sit down with me, eat with me, come to my house, but secretly hate me because I corrected you, or for something I don’t even know about.

Grudges change people’s spirit. A brother who was one way all the time is suddenly changing, and he is carrying secret hatred. That is between you and God, but God says don’t come before him praying three times a day with secret hatred. And don’t wait for the day of atonement to call that brother; fix it.

“But thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself”. Love your brother the way you love yourself.

“Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned”. When you carry grudges, secret hatred, you condemn yourself.

Brothers carry grudges against brothers, brothers carry grudges against leaders without them even knowing, wives carry grudges against husbands and husbands against wives. But whoever carries a grudge, secret hatred, is in danger of hellfire, as Christ said. You have to fix it and resolve it.

sense.text: “He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord”. As we read, thou shalt not avenge nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people. If your brother did something evil to you and you go back and do evil to him, God will bring vengeance on you. “And he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.” God will remember your sin any time you take vengeance.

“Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee”. Put emphasis on the hurt. People are going to hurt you. Wives might hurt their husbands, husbands their wives. A brother might step out and commit fornication on his wife, and she is going to feel hurt. A brother might carry a false report to leadership and lie on you, and it hurts. But God says forgive thy neighbour the hurt. Your neighbour first and foremost is your spouse; your neighbour is your brother, your race, your people. We have to learn to forgive each other.

“So shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest.” That is the only way God will forgive you when you pray. When you sin against your God, you hurt him; he is a jealous God. Yet your brother did ought against you and you can’t forgive him, but you want God to forgive you?

In this truth there has been much hurt from people, enough to say, I ain’t messing with none of these dudes no more. But you have to forgive. The Bishop taught years ago the three trials of faith: personal, marital and congregational. Congregational is when someone among you offends you; marital is when your husband says something hurtful. Will you forgive, or shut yourself down and carry secret hatred? Each of us has to decide whether we will apply what this Bible says.
“One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord?” You carry secret hatred against somebody, and you want God to forgive you?

“He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and doth he ask forgiveness of his own sins?” You don’t even show mercy to a man who is just like you, and you want forgiveness for the evil you did.

“If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins?” To nourish hatred is to feed it secretly: you keep talking about it, I can’t stand that, he did this to me again. If you hold on to it and say, I will never forgive you, not until I die, the Lord will say, then you will die with that hatred.

“Remember thy end, and let enmity cease”. Let hatred cease. We all have to die eventually. What sense is there in living on this earth hating everybody all the time, when eventually I die like everybody else and have to go before my maker? Let hatred go. “Remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments.”

“Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour”: don’t bear secret hatred towards your neighbour. “Remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.” Ignorance is when your brother is ignorant, he doesn’t understand. When somebody does something hurtful or stupid to you, you have to wink at it.

precepts.why:
This explains winking at ignorance. “Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth”. You poke my eye, I poke out yours; you knock out my tooth, I knock out yours. That was the law.

“But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.” That is winking at ignorance.

Turning the other cheek does not mean you stand there and let somebody abuse you and beat you up. That is the Christian way of thinking. Somebody tries to punch you in the face, you better block that; self-defence is right. What Christ is saying is be willing to forgive that person.

This is the key thing with repentance. “Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him”. If your brother did evil against you, rebuke him: bro, you were wrong for what you did, don’t do that again.

“And if he repent, forgive him.” The key word is if he repent. Forgiveness comes with repentance: for me to forgive you, you have to repent and say, I’m sorry.

If he will not repent, the Bible shows how to deal with him: bring two or three witnesses; if he won’t hear them, bring him before the congregation; if he won’t hear the congregation, deal with him as an heathen and a publican. Cut him off.

“Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” That is four hundred and ninety times. If he comes and acknowledges what he did wrong and says he is sorry, you have to forgive him. You cannot say, I don’t think he really repented, so I’m not forgiving him. You want a good conscience before God.

But forgiveness and repentance go both ways. A sister tells another sister her personal business in confidence, and she goes gossiping. You rebuke her, she says I’m sorry, and you must forgive her. But would you still tell her your personal business? You would be an idiot. She broke your trust, and she has to win it back. When you hurt somebody and they forgive you, you have to prove yourself to them again and gain back their trust.

“So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.” From your hearts, not from your mouth. You can say I forgive you while deep down you are still carrying secret hatred, a grudge for what that person did, and you don’t want to let it go even though they said they were sorry.

To forgive from your heart is to forgive and forget: you don’t hold on to it anymore, you heal from the hurt they did to you. If you don’t forgive from the heart, the Lord will destroy you. And the Lord sees your heart, whether you really forgave that person.

“A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.” If you lie on somebody and offend them, it is going to be hard to win back that person’s trust, but you have to try. And if that brother or sister sincerely forgave you, they will open the gates back up and let you in.

So in offence and forgiveness both parties have work to do. The one who forgives must make sure they forgive from the heart, and the one who was forgiven has to win back the love of that person.

sense.text:
“Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone”. If somebody does something evil to you, don’t come to leadership; go to that person alone. You only come to the leaders if that person won’t hear you. If the deacon goes to him first, the person says, why did you have to go to the deacon, you could have just told me, and now a bunch of confusion starts. The Lord is showing us how to deal with problems.

“If he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.” If he says, yes, I was wrong, I shouldn’t have done that, you have won that person.

“But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” He doesn’t want to hear you; he doesn’t want to acknowledge his fault.

“And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church”: this brother does not want to repent, so bring him to the church. “But if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” Deliver him unto Satan. Don’t deal with him.
“Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven”. The congregation and the leaders have power to bind people on earth. Keep playing games.

precepts.why:
This is why the Lord shows us how to deal with offences. “Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come”. People will offend each other. Don’t come to this truth thinking nobody will offend you. Leaders offend people too, and when told, say, I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to offend you. The key thing is you can’t hold it inside.

Why must offences come? To prove us, to see if we will apply God’s laws. Offences make everybody stronger and better: when a brother says this offended me, you learn to be more mindful how you deal with certain brothers. But if you are not of the elect, those offences will take you out of the truth: she said this to me, he said that, I ain’t coming back to the school no more. Leaders sit back and watch how brothers and sisters deal with it, and smile when they apply the law, because they are growing. That is how we tell who is approved, who is real in this truth. Offences come to teach us, to make us stronger, and to weed out the fake people among us.

How you deal with the offence decides whether you get the kingdom. Somebody may do evil to you, then go to the Lord and be sorry, while you never forgive, and you don’t get the kingdom.

“But woe to that man by whom the offence cometh! Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee”.

“Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil”.

Charity thinketh no evil. Evil surmising destroys many. Satan talks in your mind, in your ears. But if you are applying the law, love thy neighbour as thyself, which is charity, you will not think evil: probably that brother didn’t mean it like that, probably that sister didn’t mean it like that. And if they did mean it as evil, God knows the heart, and the Lord will deal with it.

Satan always attacks us first in the mind. He plants seeds and thoughts: I don’t think that sister likes you, I don’t think that brother likes you, I don’t think the deacon likes me, why does he be rolling like that? That is where the fight begins, and that is where you have to destroy him, before it manifests in your actions. You literally have to repeat God’s commandments in your head: charity thinketh no evil. That is how you fight.

“Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.” To admonish is to warn. The thing you heard, or thought he did, he may not have done. Go to him first. And if he did it, tell him, don’t ever do that again, that’s wrong.

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again.” Sometimes the person didn’t say it, or said it but didn’t mean it the way you took it.

“Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.” Many times people are lying: that brother said this about you. Don’t believe everything you hear. Years ago it was said of a brother that he had a Christian spirit on him, and in 2018 a man leaving the truth went and told him, trying to plant evil in his head. But that brother came straight to the deacon and asked, did you say that? Yes, because the way you move is some Christian stuff; you’ve got to man up, be a soldier, be militant-minded. When leaders say things it is never to destroy you, but to make you better. He understood and didn’t carry it. He could have secretly hated, but he came. That is how you can tell who is real: trials have to come.

“There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart”. Something might come off wrong, but they didn’t mean anything bad in it. “And who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?” Everybody offends with what they say. What matters is how you deal with it: carry secret hatred, a grudge, or go and talk, and they say, damn, I didn’t mean it that way, I’m sorry, and it’s done. Many brothers have left the truth because a root of bitterness sprang up inside them, and bitterness usually comes from offence or correction.

“Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him”. Warn him first before you snatch him up by his neck. Find out if he said it or did it before threatening to knock his head off. This is negroes we are talking about. “And not being angry, give place to the law of the most High.” Give place to forgiveness: the brother might repent and say I’m sorry. If you go threatening him, his ego might flare up and you are both going back and forth.

“The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him”.

sense.text: “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink”. It is not saying let nobody judge me if I commit adultery or eat pork and shrimp. It is talking about meat offerings and drink offerings. “Or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days”: because we did meat offerings and drink offerings on the holy days.

“Which are a shadow of things to come”. All these things we did are a shadow of things to come. Today is the day of atonement, and the real thing behind the day of atonement is Christ. “But the body is of Christ.”

precepts.why:
This explains the meat and the drink. “Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.” When Christ said that, many went away from following him: this dude is crazy, he wants us to eat him. That is why you have to be spiritual in this truth. Christ did that on purpose to weed out the flock; it was an offence to them.

“For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.” So when Paul says let no man judge you in meat or in drink, the drink is the drink offering that was poured, which is wine, representing Christ’s blood, and the meat offering, the body of the lamb, represents Christ’s body.

“Take, eat; this is my body.” “Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.”

The wine is his blood, which is the new testament, the new covenant. The body is the sacrifice. He became the sacrifice for us.

The first tabernacle “was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings”.

The meats and drinks are the sacrifices we did and the wine, the drink offering we poured all the time. They could not make us perfect. It all represented Christ coming and dying for us: the new covenant, Christ giving his life, his blood. The wine is Christ’s blood; the body of the lamb represents Christ’s body. That is the meat and drink of Colossians 2:16.

sense.text: “By whom we have now received the atonement.” Through Jesus Christ we have received the atonement. Jesus Christ is our atonement. The lamb that used to be killed for the atonement, that is Christ. Atonement means to make amends: he is the one who makes amends for us to God, through his blood and through his body. That is how we make amends to God today.

“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned”. The one man is Adam, the first man. Because of Adam’s sin, death came upon all of us, and that is why we need an atonement.

precepts.why: Here is why Christ became our atonement, and that the Most High spoke of it from the beginning. “Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people.” Then: “The first man knew her not perfectly”. The first man is Adam. Adam did not know wisdom perfectly, meaning Adam committed sin.

“For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” The first Adam had a wicked heart, transgressed, and was overcome. And all of us that came from Adam, because of his fall and his sin, are born with that sinful nature inside us too.

That is the first man who knew not wisdom perfectly, and it is by that one man that sin entered into the world.

sense.text:
This is the prophecy of Christ being our atonement. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman”. Enmity is hatred, between Satan and the woman. “And between thy seed and her seed”: Satan’s seed, which is Esau, and her seed, which is Israel. That is good against evil.

“It shall bruise thy head”. The woman is Eve, and Eve’s head was Adam. It shall bruise thy head is Adam coming back and dying for the mistake he made in the beginning. Because he sinned, sin came in and we all have to die; so Adam came and fixed that mistake. This is God prophesying Adam, the son of God, coming and dying for our sins.

“And thou shalt bruise his heel.” Adam is going to take down Satan and his children. Jacob grabbed hold of Esau’s heel; that represents Adam destroying the devil and his children. That is what we are waiting on right now: for our king to return and take them down by their heel.

precepts.why: Who is Adam? “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” Adam was the son of God. So when we read that Jesus Christ was the son of God, the apostles understood all that meant: that he is Adam, literally the son of God. He was made flesh in Genesis, and he was made flesh in the time of the apostles.

“Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin”. The him here is Christ, Adam. Remember what the Lord said in the beginning: it shall bruise thy head. This is Adam being bruised. His soul made an offering for sin: that is atonement.

Read back in the chapter: “He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief”. Christ was hated. “Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.” That is Christ.

And on: “by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.” That is atonement: the prophecy of Adam, Christ, coming and dying and bearing our iniquities.

“Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?” This is all talking about Adam, the son of God, coming and dying: the firstborn given for the transgression.

“For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” This goes back to Genesis 3:15, Micah 6:7 and Isaiah 53: it pleased the Lord to bruise him, when he made his soul an offering for sin.

Through Adam everybody died. Then Adam came back, walked perfectly, and fixed it, and we are all going to live. He came, died and sacrificed himself for us; he became that atonement for us. That is our head being bruised.
“For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.” Christ knew no sin, yet he was made to be sin for us. He became that sacrifice for us.

“For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God”. He was perfect, but he suffered for our sins. He was just, and he suffered for the unjust, and the unjust is us.

“Being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”. The Lord brought him back to life. He was put to death in the flesh and came back in the spirit; he changed, because he walked perfect. “By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison”.

“Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus”. That is how we get redemption.

“Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past”. Propitiation is a covering, an atoning sacrifice. He is our atoning and our sacrifice. On this day we celebrate that Christ is our atonement; the sacrifices we did all the time were always a representation of Christ.

“And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous”. An advocate is a lawyer: if you sin, you have a lawyer. “And he is the propitiation for our sins”: he is the atonement for our sins. That is how we get atonement, through Christ.

“Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.” Propitiation means atonement: he sent his son to be the atonement for our sin.

“Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.” We are to love one another.

sense.text: “For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.” The bodies of the animals brought for sin were taken outside the camp, outside the congregation, and burnt there.

“Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.” The bullock or the lamb was burnt outside the camp to sanctify the people with the blood, and so Jesus Christ suffered outside the city of Jerusalem. Golgotha, the place of a skull, was a place of execution outside the city. Paul was heavy; he understood these things.

“Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.” Let us go forth and serve Christ without the rest of Israel. Bearing his reproach is bearing the hatred that comes on us for following Christ. The world is going to hate us. If you think this is a love fest, no: you are going to be hated.
“For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.” He said we have no continuing city because Jerusalem was about to be destroyed by the Romans, and Paul understood that.

precepts.why:
This is where the scripture says it. “If a soul shall sin through ignorance against any of the commandments of the Lord”: if Israel commits sin. Then: “Even the whole bullock shall he carry forth without the camp unto a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn him on the wood with fire”.

This bullock represents Christ: carried forth without the camp and burnt on the wood. That is what Paul is pointing to in Hebrews 13.

“Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away. And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha”.

They led him out of the city. And what was he carrying? The cross: the wood. The bullock was burnt on the wood without the camp, and Christ bore the wood and suffered without the gate.

sense.text: “For the wages of sin is death”. If you commit sin, what price do you pay? A wage is a payment, and the payment for sin is death: it is your blood. “But the gift of God is eternal life”.

precepts.why:
“And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you. For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall be surely put to death”. “His blood shall be upon him”: you are going to die. There is no forgiveness for that; what is owed is your life. The wages of sin is death.

“The adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.” So what is supposed to happen to most of us? We all came from all walks of life, and we are all supposed to be dead. We have a price on our head. That is why atonement is so important, and why Christ coming and dying for us is so important.

“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come”, “Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.” The holy place is where the Father is. He redeemed all of us.

“How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” He offered himself to God as a sacrifice for our sins, because of the love he has for us, and because of what we read in Genesis 3:15: he knew that in the beginning through him we all fell, so he came to fix it. And all his sons were predestined. It is not a coincidence that we are waking up to this truth: we were all with him in the beginning. He knows his sheep.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament”. “For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.”

“Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.” This is the blood covenants. A covenant is an agreement or a promise, and both covenants we entered with the Lord were with blood. When Moses had spoken every precept, “he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people”. We entered into a blood covenant, and there is no coming out of it but by death: break that covenant, and you die. That is why the one who curses his father or mother has his own blood upon him.

“And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.” None of us can be forgiven unless blood is shed. If you commit sin, the Lord wants your blood. So Christ, through the eternal Spirit, came and shed his blood for us, so we could have immortal life. He became our atonement: he makes amends for us. That is how serious this feast is.

sense.text: “And thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years unto thee, seven times seven years; and the space of the seven sabbaths of years shall be unto thee forty and nine years.” Seven times seven is forty-nine years.

“Then shalt thou cause the trumpet of the jubile to sound on the tenth day of the seventh month”. Today is the tenth day of the seventh month, the day of atonement. So atonement is also jubilee. “In the day of atonement shall ye make the trumpet sound throughout all your land.” The trumpet was sounded on the day of atonement to gather the people. Jubilee was kept on the same day as atonement every seven years, and the fiftieth year is also a sabbath.

“And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you”. To proclaim liberty: that is the jubilee, the release. This is another level to atonement.

“If thy brother be waxen poor, and hath sold away some of his possession, and if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold.” One part of the jubilee is possession. If you sold your family inheritance because you were poor, one of your family members could come and buy it back.

“And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner”. This is not chattel slavery. This is a brother who is poor and comes to work for you, like a nanny or a worker in your field: he is employed by you, a servant. We cannot use our own people as bondservants, only as hired servants. You deal with a heathen differently than with your own brother.

That is the scripture that says servants obey your masters. Christians and atheists twist it to say the Bible tells negroes to obey the white man. But the master is your brother, the employer: obey your employer.

“He shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile”. The year of jubilee is the day of atonement, seven times seven years.

“And then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.” When that trumpet blows, every man packs up and goes. All of this goes into what Christ is going to do; it is no coincidence. We are going to return to the possessions of our fathers soon.

“For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.” We are God’s servants. We are not supposed to be anybody’s slaves, not even our own brothers’. Jubilee is God freeing his servants.

precepts.why:
“At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release.” The release is jubilee. “Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the Lord’s release.”

If you lent a million dollars and the year of jubilee comes, you are not getting it back, and you can’t fight your brother down for it. That money is dead. In the year of jubilee all debts are paid. It is the Lord’s release, and it comes on the day of atonement.

“And if thy brother, an Hebrew man, or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee, and serve thee six years; then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free from thee.” “Thou shalt not let him go away empty”: make sure his pockets are fat and he is good when you send him away.

So the year of release, the jubilee, is all debts being forgiven. When that seventh year comes and the day of atonement arrives, whatever you owe anybody is forgiven.

“Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought”. Your poor brother asks to borrow five grand, and you think, it’s a couple more weeks before the release, I ain’t going to get it back. Now your eye is evil.

“And he cry unto the Lord against thee, and it be sin unto thee.” “Thou shalt surely give him, and thine heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him”. Do it with a cheerful heart, for the Lord loves a cheerful giver; and the scripture that says lose thy money for thy friend goes into this jubilee. “For this thing the Lord thy God shall bless thee in all thy works”. God will bless you when you do good and help the poor. We are to deal right with each other and help each other.

“Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.” Christ has released us, made us free. That is what the jubilee, the atonement, means: the year of release.

“If ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.” If you go back to the law of animal sacrifice, Christ will profit you nothing. “He is a debtor to do the whole law.” If you do animal sacrifice you owe a big debt, and remember, the year of jubilee is about the forgiveness of debts. “Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.”

“After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come.” “And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.”

What is the debt we owe the Lord? Our life, because we were supposed to be dead, and he became our atonement. So we ask him to forgive us that debt, the same way we forgive those that owe us. That goes into the jubilee, the year of release, when whatever anybody owes is forgiven. Whatever we owe the Lord is going to be forgiven on that day of atonement, that jubilee.

“Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.” We owe the Lord a big debt. That is why when we pray we ask him to forgive us the debt we owe him, the same way we forgive the debts people owe us.

This is why Christ gave this analogy. One “which owed him ten thousand talents”, and “his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.” That is us: we were sold, we went into slavery. The lord is the Lord.

“The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all. Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.” He loosed him: that goes into jubilee.

But the same servant found a fellowservant “which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest.” Where’s my money? And when his fellowservant begged patience, “he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt.”

“O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?” You owed ten million and were forgiven; he owed you a hundred, and you couldn’t show him compassion. We have to be able to forgive each other, forgiving debts as our debts are forgiven.

“And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors”. The tormentors are the angels, the reapers. “So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.” Forgive your brother his trespass.

sense.text:
“But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation? And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds”. This man was a thief about to be killed beside Christ. He acknowledged his sin: we are justly being put to death for what we did.

“But this man hath done nothing amiss.” That shows he knew Christ was innocent. He had been following him and knew his teachings, the same way some online right now know the teachings of the Lord but are still in evil.

“Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.” “Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.”

That is the power of the Lord. The Most High can forgive whatever evil you did; you have to acknowledge him and keep his commandments. That is why you never look down on anyone, no matter what they are going through: you don’t know what the Most High could do with anyone. We have brothers locked up doing forty years, eighty years, and our people need the word of the Most High.

Things are getting very crazy in the world. All over Europe they are rising up and saying, we don’t want to be around your negroes no more. In America they are saying, we don’t want you immigrants here no more. Things are changing, God is doing his thing on this earth, and we have to be ready for what is coming: we need God to send us labourers, to strengthen us, and to protect us for the wars to come. We have to get it right, become stronger, and let the fast count: offend less.
